Author: @augmented2nd666
Content:
They are illegal on streets where I am (Canada), not to mention no way of insuring here either, not sure about the USA, I'm guessing its different state to state. I'm seeing no license plates on them in videos. 
We have them here, I've seen the odd one on the street, accelerating like a Tesla and bobbing and weaving through traffic. They will get hit, people will be annoyed with them faster than motorcycles already annoy people for stupid stuff, and people dont like the fact they are evading paying insurance when the rest of us in vehicles are. Not to mention when in an accident they dont have insurance so if they cause any "accidents" and injure anyone else, theres no coverage. And like Ebikes, these clowns will probably also interchange themselves from motorvehicle (supposedly adhering to road rules) to non motor vehicle/pedestrian whenever they feel like it, using crosswalks to avoid waiting, flat out using sidewalks or bike lanes when they want to, cutting through parks and walking/cycling paths is an obvious one, all at ridiculous speed.
Trails already have a problem with the Ebike crowd, mostly the ones on surron throttle ones but some modify their mountain Ebikes to have a throttle and boost over 40kmph uphill. When you dont have to really exert force to get momentum it often has the rider in less control due to carelessness of conservation of momentum because its unearned. This results in someone boosting around our trails at ridiculous speeds even uphill with complete disregard, disassociation and disrespect for those that have used the path for decades with their own power, whether walking, trail running or pedalling. This makes for very dangerous conditions on the trails, imagine a motorbike riding non motorbike trails, except its nearly silent.
There needs to be way stricter regulation on these devices, and specific usage designation, I see some places have put up no motorized signs on trails and paths, but the Ebike people and these Eunicycles will state they dont have a gas motor despite the sign saying the broader term, an electric motor is still a motor. And as for streets, police need some better measures to deal with this, as I'm sure its very difficult to track one down without identification, heck, some could be kids without a drivers license for all we know seeing as they just ride them without insurance wherever they feel like.
If all else fails, just do open season on em, they'll learn quick, if they dont want to have insurance for road use, they wont be using the road much longer.

Author: @TerrenceColeman-g7l
Content: I have a unicycle and used it daily to commute to campus VT. Surprisingly, Potholes aren’t the issues it’s actually the rider. EUC is all about balance control and going over potholes causes your balances to be out of wack “causing most people to fall” but the more experienced EUC riders the ones that you think of flying down the road going crazy fast while having a straight face never fall from these. Something’s we do is we learn roads so we know where they’re at or were extremely aware of everything so we look hundreds of feet in front us to locate any obstacles. Or in a lot cases we look up and down constantly especially on roads we’ve never been on. Almost every fall I saw on the video was a person looking straight ahead going over obstacles that could cause you to eat shit if you aren’t careful and them eating shit lmao. Literally the best way to go over any obstacles on a EUC is to just crouch a little but, basically bend your knees before hitting the obstacles so it doesn’t cause you to lose balances. But once again it’s a trick only the real experiences EUC use.

Author: @maxatrillionfatstacks
Content: My friend commuted for a while on one of these for a bit after getting a DUI, his only went 45mph and he was already crazy talented on a regular unicycle, he could take like 6 foot drops on a uni no problem. I don't see it as any more dangerous than bicycles or motorcycles aside from the accessibility of speed for people that don't know how to ride a uni. Honestly those one wheel electric skateboards are way more sketchy to me because your feet are in front and behind of the drive wheel rather than next to it. Most of them don't have suspension but the tire and your knees cushion most bumps. Some do have suspension but I've seen people hit huge jumps on ones that don't have suspension. The few times my friend that commuted on one did get hurt was trail riding it and trying to bail but having it give a burst of power and twisting his ankle and with any type of electric thing that relies of its power for balance as well thats the main sketchy part, having too much power delivered or the power cutting out causes lots of crashes and there's usually saftey features in place to prevent that but they're not 100% reliable.

Author: @TheFojacko
Content:
Just get yourself an electric scooter at this point, pretty much all of the accidents are due to lack of balance, the handlebars pretty much solve that issue entirely. You can push an electric scooter without complete fear of bumps and changes in terrain throwing you off, you can also recover from a potential fall so much easier.

Obviously people will see this opinion as an attack on their hobby, but what i'm trying to say is that most of us don't want their hobby to potentially kill them. I personally believe that it is a train of thought that demands professional attention, at some point you gotta start asking why exactly you crave such intense amounts of adrenaline. The usual answer of "it makes me feel alive" is what i'm talking about with the whole "professional attention" thing, if you need the threat of death to "feel alive" then what do you feel the other 99% of the time?

Author: @TurtleSauceGaming
Content:
I am a really good driver.  Like, I believe you can't control others, but you can absolutely see people's stupid decisions coming, and I've avoided countless accidents that way.  Like, not just defensive driving and slowing down, but just being properly aware of what's around you.  I remember being in a bad cluster of traffic on a highway.  Everyone's going 70+, and I'm trying to merge into an exit lane while people are merging out of it.  I see a clear opening, but you get that feeling of "no, something's not right."  Sure enough, from about three or four car lengths back, some guy comes flying up (through cars going 70, so he's easily going 80+ in this tight pack) and cuts into that spot.  And mind you, this all through mirrors.  It's about pattern recognition and knowing how to use your mirrors, plus having them setup properly.  
All this, and I still ain't taking a fucking unicycle 70+ mph.  It just ain't worth it.

Author: @CriticalPixel
Content: I ride all the time, potholes aren't really a problem if your careful, the larger wheels can handle them easily.... actually easier to handle when you are going faster because it lessens the bump and suspention wheels just soak it up. As long as your aware of the road surface (which you get to learn pretty quickly) when riding on the roads its generally fine with skill. Speed actually helps because going at traffic speeds is safer when your not being overtaken by cars passing by, even cyclist have that danger. If you fall  you fall forward onto your hands and knees and slide rather than sideways and hit your head like a scooter or bike. Thats why we mostly use beefy kneepads and wrist guards. I've known people crash at 40mph + and only take minor injuries. Cars are the thing thats the most dangerous. Its is a very dangerous thing to ride, but not nearly as dangerous as people think. Ride with skill and care for others and be aware of everything.

Author: @asherq8646
Content:
Had to comment again to answer some questions presented in the video:
1. Since it is auto balancing, you only have to balance side to side - same concept as a bicycle or scooter. 
2. Since your weight is centered over 1 (large) tire, your contact point actually provides a ton of grip.
3. There are safety mechanisms such as speed alarms and tilt back that prevent you from pushing the wheel too hard
4. The larger diameter tire makes all the difference in the types of terrain you can traverse, EUCs absolutely crush anything with smaller diameter wheels (scooter, board, one wheel). 
5. They are extremely durable. My v12 pro has been slammed into concrete more times than I can count. Just has a few scuffs - they are made to crash because they know you’ll take a few tumbles during the learning phase.

Author: @czpetr1234
Content:
It's much less dangerous than most people think. I have well over 10k kilometers, roads and offroad, and the only road "crash" I had was me falling into ditch due to strong wind, but that was rider error because I froze.

Most EUCs have fairly good suspension, pretty large wheel and insanely strong electric motor that's trying to balance you at all times. You can pretty much ignore potholes.

Crahses are mostly fine as long as you don't hit something, most riders wear motorcycle gear and there are no handlebars to get hurt by. EUC is also much less dangerous than car/motorcycle in a crash.

Then there are people overtaking cars and riding like idiots in traffic, but that's people problem, not EUC problem.

Author: @SirRafix
Content:
Here are the reasons these electric unicycles will never work as an extreme sport: 

It is too heavy of an object to pop with. (lift up)
You can't pop this thing without a nose/tail and a second wheel atleast. (you can possibly bounce it, but it would take great efford, which in turn makes doing tricks much harder.
It easily breaks or ever explodes, because electric.
Keeping balance on this takes much more effort and energy than standing on a skateboard or inlines
Super expensive for something that's going to endure a daily beating
You can not do grinds, slides, manuals, flips, grabs, liptricks. Maybe some very limited freestyle on flatground, without any pops.

What else... Ah yes. You can't really skate transitions with this thing. Imagine dropping into a vert ramp with a unicycle. If it is possible, than that alone would be a trick in itself.
Stairs are a no, rails are a no, curbs and ledges are a no, ramps are a no. This thing is literally only good for races.

I've been skateboarding for 30 years, so take my word for it or don't, but this is what I think about unicycle extreme sports.

Author: @FUZ2706
Content:
I own one of these and I love it,  best mode of transportation, so fun!

To answer some questions in the video:
-They come with and without suspension depending on price
-They do have safety measures to keep you from going too fast, like pedal tilt back, beeps letting you know you're going to fast (usually customizable in app settings)
-Most of the accidents from potholes are actually rider error from not keeping knees bent
-If you fall with it, the euc usually will survive most of the time (98%)
-There are EUC's that are made for off road and jumps and ones made for street and on road.
-They vary in weight, wheel size, battery size/range, speed, price
-The speed is controlled with your weight, lean forward to go forward, back to stop/go back.

Author: @jimmux_v0
Content:
I've been riding EUC a couple of years now. It's getting kind of funny how everyone always thinks a little rock will wipe you out, but I ride MTB trails regularly. They have come a long way lately with the power and suspension.

I feel much safer commuting on one compared to a bike, because the speed and agility has helped me avoid situations that would have wrecked me before. Good gear also does a lot to minimise injury if something does go wrong.

But most of all, they just feel amazing to ride. Nothing else will get you feeling connected to the machine on this level. Give it a go if you're even slightly curious. It's easier than it looks.

Author: @GioSpagnoli
Content:
I ride an EUC called the Inmotion V11 that goes 34mph. They can take quite a betting when you fall, most of the pieces that would need to be replaced are inexpensive. Most that go over 30mph have suspension, the slower ones for the final mile rides normally don't.

They are pretty safe when compared to other personal electric vehicles like electric skateboards or one wheels. But most times it in the hand of the rider to control their wheel as best they can.

I've ridden ones that go 50mph and they are so stable at high speeds as long as you are experienced.

Smaller spills don't break EUCs. Let me know if you guys have any questions.
